study_inclusion_sensitivity.scope: One existing exclusion refit; other study exclusions remain untested.

requested_output_grid_sensitivity_at_fro.interpretation: This compares requested-output-grid extrema at the same frozen parameter vector; it does not itself refit the objective or prove continuous-time extrema.

twofold_acoustic_weight_refit.weight_change: Multiply all acoustic residual components by sqrt(2), doubling their combined squared-residual weight relative to pharmacological components.

pike_bosher.weighting: Baseline-relative EP error / (10 mV * sqrt(anchors per dose curve)).

asakuma.weighting: Resistance ratio error / 0.2; baseline-minus-nadir EP error / 10 mV.

rybak.weighting: EP and K group-mean reduction errors / reported SE; covariance unknown.

wang_1992.weighting: Baseline-relative EP error / (3 mV * sqrt(anchors per sound level)).

wang_1990.weighting: Separate-cohort EP difference error / (5 mV * sqrt(number of cohorts)).

salt_table_iii.weighting: Local-episode delta EP / (3 mV * sqrt(3 episodes)); no SD/n precision; timing window is hypothetical.

salt_figure_3.weighting: Each Figure 3 series uses baseline-relative errors divided by 3 mV or 3 mM times sqrt(points in that series); illustrative deterministic weights, not a likelihood. Fig. 3 is one paired EP/K animal.

twofold_acoustic_weight_refit.interpretation: A single, deliberately simple weight perturbation; it is not a likelihood, confidence interval, or comprehensive robustness analysis.

fine_grid_refit.interpretation: The 0.025-min refit tests endpoint-grid sensitivity locally from the frozen candidate; it is not an event-based extremum calculation or a new primary fit.

limitations: Historical traces are digitized and serially correlated; target count is not independent information.
The alternative weight is one analyst-selected sensitivity perturbation, not a probability model.
The endpoint-grid comparisons use requested output samples, not continuous-time events.
Neither refit establishes parameter identifiability, uncertainty, global optimality, or predictive validity.
